statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of Alcohol or Drugs
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
Upon the ways of this state open to the public
While under the influence of alcohol, a dangerous drug, any other drug, or any combination
Or had an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more
mandatory_minimum: 24 consecutive hours imprisonment (first); 7 days (second); 30 days (third); 1 year (fourth+)
enhancements: BAC of 0.16 or higher (aggravated DUI under § 61-8-442)
notes: Montana uses a 10-year lookback for prior offenses. Implied consent under § 61-8-402. ACE (Alcohol Compliance Enforcement) program may be required. License suspension 6 months first offense.

elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs
BAC of 0.08 or higher, or impairment of ability to safely operate
No prior DUI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 24 consecutive hours imprisonment; completion of alcohol education course
notes: Court may suspend all but 24 hours. Chemical dependency assessment required. License suspension 6 months. Eligible for probationary license after 45 days.

elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs
BAC of 0.08 or higher, or impairment of ability to safely operate
One or more prior DUI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 7 days (second); 30 days (third); 1 year (fourth+, 13 months no parole eligibility)
notes: Second offense: 1-year license suspension. Third: 1-year suspension. Fourth+: 1-year suspension plus vehicle forfeiture possible. 24/7 sobriety program may be ordered.

statute_title: DUI — Dangerous Drug or Other Drug
offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of a dangerous drug
Or under the influence of any other drug that rendered defendant incapable of safely driving
Or under the combined influence of alcohol and any drug
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: Montana has no per se drug limits. Prosecution must show actual impairment. Includes prescription medications. Drug Recognition Expert (DRE) evaluations commonly used.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense within 3 years
notes: Common plea-down from DUI. 5 points on driving record. Second offense within 3 years carries enhanced penalties.

statute_title: Duty to Stop — Accident Involving Injury or Death
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage to attended vehicle
Defendant failed to stop immediately at the scene
Defendant failed to give name, address, registration, and render aid
notes: Failure to stop at accident involving injury or death is a felony. Property damage only accidents require stopping and exchanging information but are misdemeanors.

elements: Defendant operated a vehicle
In a negligent manner
Causing the death of another person
enhancements: DUI involved (§ 61-8-465 — vehicular homicide while under the influence)
notes: Montana charges DUI-related vehicular deaths under § 61-8-465 as aggravated DUI resulting in death (up to 30 years). Non-DUI vehicular deaths charged as negligent homicide under § 45-5-104.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
By criminal negligence
While operating a motor vehicle
notes: Montana does not have a separate vehicular manslaughter statute. Vehicular deaths are charged as negligent homicide. DUI-related deaths are charged under § 61-8-465 with enhanced penalties.

statute_title: Driving While Privilege to Drive Suspended or Revoked
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a public highway
Defendant's driving privilege was suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge or notice of the suspension or revocation
mandatory_minimum: 2 days (second); 10 days (third+)
notes: Applies to both Montana residents and nonresidents whose privilege has been suspended. Additional suspension of 1 year added to existing suspension.

statute_title: Fleeing From or Eluding a Peace Officer
offense_class: Misdemeanor (basic); Felony (if creating substantial risk of death or serious bodily injury)
elements: A peace officer gave a visual or audible signal to stop
Defendant operated a motor vehicle
Defendant willfully fled or attempted to elude the officer
Defendant knew or should have known the signal was from a peace officer
enhancements: Creating substantial risk of death or serious bodily injury (felony)
notes: Officer must be in uniform and use clearly marked vehicle or red/blue lights. Felony eluding applies when flight creates high risk of harm.

elements: Defendant possessed a dangerous drug
Drug is listed in Montana Dangerous Drug Act schedules
Possession was without a valid prescription or lawful authority
enhancements: Prior drug felony (2 years–40 years under § 45-9-101)
Possession in or near a school zone
notes: Montana classifies drugs as 'dangerous drugs' in visual, narcotic, or anabolic steroid schedules. First offense treatment court diversion may be available.

elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
Without lawful authority
Not within the Montana Marijuana Regulation and Taxation Act provisions
notes: Montana legalized recreational marijuana for adults 21+ effective January 1, 2022 (I-190/HB 701). Possession over the legal limit or by those under 21 remains criminal.

elements: Defendant possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II dangerous drug in Montana
Possession was without lawful authority
enhancements: Possession in or near a school zone
notes: No minimum quantity for possession charge. Larger quantities may support distribution charges under § 45-9-101.

elements: Defendant possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II dangerous drug
Possession was without lawful authority
enhancements: Possession in or near a school zone
notes: Methamphetamine is a major enforcement priority in Montana. Treatment courts widely available for first-time offenders.

penalty_max: Life (subsequent offense); 25 years (first offense, to a minor)
elements: Defendant sold, bartered, exchanged, gave away, or offered to sell a dangerous drug
Or defendant possessed dangerous drugs with intent to distribute
The substance was a dangerous drug under Montana law
mandatory_minimum: 1 year (first); 10 years (to minors); 2 years (second felony drug offense)
enhancements: Distribution within 1,000 feet of a school
notes: Montana's drug distribution statute is the primary trafficking charge. No separate trafficking statute — distribution covers large-scale operations.

statute_title: Criminal Distribution of Dangerous Drugs — General
elements: Defendant sold, bartered, exchanged, gave away, or offered to sell
A dangerous drug as defined by Montana law
To another person
mandatory_minimum: 1 year (first offense); 2 years (second offense)
enhancements: Distribution to a minor (enhanced mandatory minimum)
notes: Distribution includes any transfer of dangerous drugs, not just sale for profit. Offering to sell is sufficient even if no actual transfer occurs.

statute_title: Criminal Production or Manufacture of Dangerous Drugs
elements: Defendant manufactured, prepared, compounded, or processed a dangerous drug
Or defendant possessed precursor chemicals with intent to manufacture
The substance was a dangerous drug
mandatory_minimum: 1 year
notes: Separate enhanced penalties for methamphetamine production under § 45-9-132. Environmental cleanup costs may be assessed.

elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With intent to use the paraphernalia to introduce a dangerous drug into the body
Paraphernalia as defined in § 45-10-101
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor (felony under § 45-10-107)
notes: Misdemeanor for possession. Distribution of paraphernalia to a minor is a felony. Commercial sale regulated under § 45-10-105.

statute_title: Criminal Possession with Intent to Distribute
elements: Defendant possessed a dangerous drug
With intent to sell, barter, exchange, or give away the drug
Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, or other evidence
mandatory_minimum: 1 year
notes: Montana does not have a separate PWID statute — possession with intent is prosecuted under distribution (§ 45-9-101). This entry reflects the common charge as applied.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused the death of another human being
Or attempted to commit, committed, or fled after committing certain felonies and a death occurred (felony murder)
mandatory_minimum: 10 years (general); Life without parole if aggravating circumstances
notes: Montana calls first-degree murder 'deliberate homicide.' Death penalty is available but rarely imposed. Montana abolished the death penalty effective 2015 — existing sentences grandfathered.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused the death of another human being
Under circumstances that do not constitute aggravated deliberate homicide
notes: Montana does not formally separate murder into first and second degree. Deliberate homicide covers both. Mitigating circumstances such as heat of passion reduce the sentencing range.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused the death of another
Under the influence of extreme mental or emotional stress
For which there is reasonable explanation or excuse
notes: Montana handles voluntary manslaughter through mitigated deliberate homicide under § 45-5-102. Mental or emotional stress provides mitigating factor reducing the penalty range.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
By criminal negligence
Defendant was not aware of the risk but should have been
notes: Montana's negligent homicide covers what other states call involuntary manslaughter. Includes vehicular deaths caused by negligence.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused serious bodily injury to another
Or purposely or knowingly caused bodily injury with a weapon
Or negligently caused bodily injury with a weapon
Or purposely or knowingly caused reasonable apprehension of serious bodily injury through use of a weapon
mandatory_minimum: 2 years (if weapon used); 4 years (if serious bodily injury to a partner/family member)
enhancements: Use of a weapon (mandatory minimum 2 years)
Against a partner or family member (mandatory minimum 4 years under § 45-5-206)
Against a peace officer or emergency responder
notes: Montana's aggravated assault covers both weapon-involved and serious injury assaults. Mandatory minimums apply for weapon use and domestic situations.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused bodily injury to another
Or negligently caused bodily injury to another with a weapon
notes: Montana defines assault as causing actual bodily injury, not just apprehension of harm. Simple assault without a weapon is a misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused bodily injury to another
Through physical contact
notes: Montana does not have a separate battery statute. Harmful or offensive physical contact is prosecuted as assault under § 45-5-201.

elements: Defendant, in the course of committing a theft
Purposely or knowingly inflicted bodily injury on another
Or used or threatened the immediate use of force upon another
enhancements: Use of a weapon or dangerous instrument
notes: Montana does not separately grade robbery. All robbery is a felony with a wide sentencing range. Use of a weapon increases likely sentence.

elements: Defendant, in the course of committing a theft
Used or threatened the immediate use of force
While armed with a weapon or dangerous instrument
mandatory_minimum: 4 years (weapon use enhancement under § 46-18-221)
enhancements: Use of a firearm (additional mandatory years under § 46-18-221)
notes: Montana charges armed robbery under the general robbery statute with weapon enhancement. Mandatory weapon enhancements under § 46-18-221 add to the base sentence.

penalty_max: Life (if victim not released unharmed); 10 years (if released unharmed)
elements: Defendant knowingly or purposely and without lawful authority
Restrained another person by secreting or holding the person in a place of isolation
Or by using or threatening to use physical force
enhancements: Victim not released unharmed in a safe place (life imprisonment possible)
notes: Aggravated kidnapping under § 45-5-303 applies when victim is held for ransom, as a shield/hostage, or to facilitate a felony. Carries up to 100 years or life.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly started a fire or caused an explosion
Which placed another person in danger of death or bodily injury
Or which damaged or destroyed an occupied structure
enhancements: Occupied structure at time of fire
Fire set for insurance fraud purposes
notes: Montana classifies arson by whether the structure was occupied and whether persons were endangered. Separate offense for negligent arson under § 45-6-104.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly attempted to cause the death of another
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward causing death
Defendant had the specific intent to kill
notes: Attempt carries the same maximum penalty as the completed offense under Montana law. Attempted deliberate homicide is punishable up to life.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused bodily injury to another
With a weapon
Or negligently caused bodily injury with a weapon
mandatory_minimum: 2 years (weapon enhancement)
enhancements: Against a partner or family member
notes: Assault with a weapon is a specific form of aggravated assault. Mandatory minimum of 2 years for any assault involving a weapon.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly obtained or exerted unauthorized control over property of another
Or obtained property by deception or threat
With the purpose of depriving the owner of the property
notes: Montana consolidated all theft offenses under § 45-6-301. Felony threshold is $1,500. Value determines offense classification.

elements: Defendant committed theft as defined in § 45-6-301
Value of property was $1,500 or more
notes: Montana does not use the term 'grand theft.' Felony theft applies when value reaches $1,500.

elements: Defendant committed theft as defined in § 45-6-301
Value of property was less than $1,500
notes: Montana does not use the term 'petty theft.' Misdemeanor theft applies when value is under $1,500.

elements: Defendant took merchandise from a retail establishment
Without paying the purchase price
With intent to deprive the merchant of the merchandise
notes: Montana prosecutes shoplifting under the general theft statute. Civil recovery by merchants also available under § 27-1-720.

elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully
In an occupied structure
With the purpose to commit an offense therein
notes: Montana's burglary statute applies to occupied structures broadly defined. Aggravated burglary under § 45-6-204(2) applies when the offender is armed or causes injury.

elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully in an occupied structure
With the purpose to commit an offense therein
The structure was a dwelling or residence
A person was present in the dwelling
enhancements: Inflicting bodily injury during the burglary
notes: Aggravated burglary applies when the offender is armed, inflicts injury, or attempts to inflict injury. Penalty is significantly enhanced over basic burglary.

elements: Defendant committed theft as defined in § 45-6-301
Property taken was a motor vehicle
Defendant intended to deprive the owner of the vehicle
enhancements: Vehicle used in commission of another felony
notes: Motor vehicle theft is always a felony in Montana regardless of vehicle value. Unauthorized use of a motor vehicle is a separate lesser offense under § 45-6-302.

elements: Defendant obtained control over stolen property
Knowing the property to have been stolen by another
With the purpose of depriving the owner of the property
notes: Montana prosecutes receiving stolen property under the general theft statute. Knowledge that property was stolen is a required element.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly injured, damaged, or destroyed property of another
Without consent of the owner
notes: Montana uses 'criminal mischief' for what other states call vandalism. Restitution commonly ordered.

elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully
In or upon the premises of another
notes: Montana requires actual knowledge of trespass or posted notice/fencing. Criminal trespass to an occupied structure carries enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly injured, damaged, or destroyed property of another
Or purposely or knowingly tampered with property of another so as to endanger persons or property
notes: Criminal mischief covers all intentional property damage. Includes tampering with utilities, communications equipment, and transportation facilities.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused bodily injury to a partner or family member
Or negligently caused bodily injury to a partner or family member with a weapon
Partner or family member includes spouse, former spouse, person with shared child, dating partner
mandatory_minimum: 24 hours (first); 72 hours (second)
enhancements: Aggravated partner assault with weapon (§ 45-5-206(2) — felony, 2–20 years)
notes: Montana has specific partner/family member assault statutes. Third offense within any time period becomes a felony. Batterers' treatment program commonly ordered.

statute_title: Partner or Family Member Assault — First Offense
elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused bodily injury to a partner or family member
First offense
mandatory_minimum: 24 hours imprisonment; participation in intervention program
notes: Mandatory minimum 24 hours imprisonment. Court must order batterers' treatment intervention program. No deferred imposition of sentence allowed for partner assault.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (general); Felony (substantial risk of death or serious bodily injury)
elements: Defendant knowingly endangered the welfare of a child
By violating a duty of care, protection, or support
Or by creating a substantial risk to the child's health or welfare
notes: Includes leaving children in dangerous situations, exposure to drug manufacturing, and DUI with child in vehicle.

elements: Defendant purposely, knowingly, or negligently caused bodily injury to a child
Child was under 14 years of age
Injury was not the result of reasonable and moderate discipline
enhancements: Prior conviction for assault on a minor
notes: Montana has a specific statute for assaults on children under 14. Reasonable parental discipline is an affirmative defense.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Felony (if prior violation within 5 years)
elements: A valid order of protection was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant purposely or knowingly violated a provision of the order
mandatory_minimum: 24 hours imprisonment
notes: Mandatory minimum 24 hours imprisonment. Prior violation within 5 years elevates to felony. Law enforcement must arrest upon probable cause of violation.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Felony (second+ or with credible threat)
elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused another person substantial emotional distress
By repeatedly following, harassing, threatening, or intimidating the victim
On more than one occasion
enhancements: Credible threat of death or bodily injury (aggravated stalking — felony)
Violation of a protective order while stalking
notes: Aggravated stalking under § 45-5-220(2) is always a felony. Includes electronic communications and cyberstalking.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly caused bodily injury to another
Or through repeated conduct caused another person substantial emotional distress
notes: Montana does not have a standalone harassment statute. Harassing conduct is typically charged as assault or stalking. Privacy in communications violations may apply under § 45-8-213.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of Older Person
elements: Defendant abused, neglected, or exploited an older person
Older person is 60 years of age or older
Defendant was a caretaker or person in a position of trust
notes: Montana's elder abuse statutes are in the social services code. Adult Protective Services investigates. Criminal prosecution under this or general assault statutes.

elements: Defendant carried a concealed weapon
In a place prohibited by law
Without a valid concealed weapons permit (where required)
enhancements: Carrying in a prohibited place (government building, school)
notes: Montana is a constitutional carry state — no permit required for most concealed carry as of 2021 (HB 102). Restrictions remain for government buildings, schools, and certain venues.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm by Convicted Person
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had been convicted of a felony
Defendant had not had firearms rights restored
mandatory_minimum: 1 year
enhancements: Use of firearm in commission of another offense
notes: Montana allows some felons to possess firearms after completing their sentence and a waiting period. Violent felony convictions have longer restrictions.

elements: Defendant carried a concealed weapon
In a place where weapons are prohibited by law
Such as a government building, school, or bank
notes: Montana's constitutional carry law still prohibits weapons in certain locations. Government buildings, schools, federal property, and certain other locations remain off-limits.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (general); Felony (if involving a firearm creating risk of death)
elements: Defendant recklessly engaged in conduct
Specifically, discharging a firearm
Which created a substantial risk of death or serious bodily injury to another
notes: Montana charges illegal discharge of firearms under reckless endangerment or specific local ordinances. Discharge in city limits commonly prosecuted.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly obtained personal identifying information of another
Without authorization of the person
Used or attempted to use the information to obtain credit, goods, services, or anything of value
notes: Montana's identity theft statute covers a broad range of personal identifying information. Restitution commonly ordered.

elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant purposely or knowingly obtained unauthorized control over the property
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Montana prosecutes embezzlement under the general theft statute. The fiduciary relationship is the distinguishing element.

elements: Defendant, with purpose to defraud
Falsely made, completed, or altered a written instrument
Or knowingly possessed a forged instrument
With intent to issue or deliver it
notes: Forgery is always a felony in Montana regardless of the value involved. Includes checks, contracts, deeds, and identification documents.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of a Credit Card or Debit Card
elements: Defendant used a credit or debit card knowing it was forged, expired, or revoked
Or defendant possessed a device for making counterfeit cards
With intent to defraud
notes: Montana addresses counterfeiting through forgery and fraud statutes. Federal counterfeiting of currency charges commonly apply.

elements: Defendant issued or passed a check or similar instrument
Knowing it would not be paid by the drawee
Or defendant had insufficient funds and failed to make good within 30 days of notice
notes: Prosecution must prove defendant knew the check would not be paid. Failure to make good within 30 days of notice creates a presumption of knowledge.

elements: Defendant knowingly presented or caused to be presented a false or fraudulent claim
For payment or benefit under an insurance policy
With intent to defraud
notes: Montana's insurance fraud statute is in the Insurance Code. Restitution and civil penalties may apply in addition to criminal penalties.

elements: Defendant used a credit card, debit card, or account number of another
Without the cardholder's authorization
To obtain goods, services, or anything of value
With intent to defraud
notes: Montana prosecutes credit card fraud under deceptive practices or theft statutes depending on the circumstances.

fine_max: $50,000 or twice the value of the property involved
elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Knowing the property involved represented proceeds of criminal activity
With intent to promote, carry on, or conceal criminal activity
notes: Montana's money laundering statute carries significant penalties. Fine may be up to twice the value of the property involved.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly obtained property of another by deception
Or created a false impression of law, value, or intention
With intent to defraud
notes: Montana's deceptive practices statute is the general fraud offense. Covers a broad range of fraudulent conduct.

elements: Defendant knowingly subjected another person to sexual contact or sexual intercourse
Without consent
mandatory_minimum: 2 years (general); 4 years (bodily injury); 25 years (victim under 16 and offender 3+ years older)
enhancements: Victim under 16 (mandatory 25 years to life under § 45-5-503)
notes: Montana's sexual assault statute covers both contact and intercourse offenses. Sexual intercourse without consent (§ 45-5-503) carries life imprisonment.

elements: Defendant knowingly had sexual intercourse with another person
Without consent of the victim
Consent was absent due to force, threat, incapacity, or other statutory circumstance
mandatory_minimum: 2 years (general); 25 years (victim under 16 and offender 3+ years older)
enhancements: Victim under 16 years of age (25 years to life)
notes: Montana calls rape 'sexual intercourse without consent.' Carries the most severe penalties in Montana's sexual offense code.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Felony (if prior conviction for sexual or violent offense)
elements: Defendant knowingly exposed genitals
Under circumstances likely to cause affront or alarm
To another person
enhancements: Prior conviction for sexual or violent offense (felony)
notes: First offense is a misdemeanor. Becomes a felony if offender has a prior sexual or violent offense conviction.

elements: Defendant engaged in or offered or agreed to engage in sexual intercourse
For compensation
Or defendant solicited another to engage in sexual intercourse for compensation
notes: Both the person soliciting and the person offering are subject to prosecution. Promoting prostitution (pimping/pandering) carries felony penalties.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed, produced, or distributed visual or print medium depicting sexual conduct by a child
Or defendant used the internet to facilitate sexual abuse of a child
mandatory_minimum: 4 years (general); 25 years (certain offenses involving children under 13)
enhancements: Production of child sexual abuse material (enhanced penalty)
notes: Montana's child exploitation statutes are among the most severe. Production and distribution carry significantly longer sentences than possession.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sexual or Violent Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sexual or violent offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register or update registration
Or defendant provided false information on the registration
enhancements: Second or subsequent failure to register
notes: Montana Sexual or Violent Offender Registration Act requires lifetime registration for certain offenses. Registration must be updated annually and upon address change.

penalty_max: Life (victim under 16); 100 years (victim 14–15 and offender 3+ years older)
elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse with a person under 16 years of age
Defendant was 3 or more years older than the victim
Consent is not a defense due to victim's age
mandatory_minimum: 4 years (victim 14–15); 25 years (victim under 14)
notes: Montana age of consent is 16. Three-year age difference is the threshold for prosecution. Victims under 14 face the most severe penalty enhancements.

elements: Defendant knowingly disturbed the peace by violent, threatening, or tumultuous conduct
Or by unreasonable noise
notes: Montana's disorderly conduct is a minor misdemeanor with minimal penalties. Often used as a catch-all for public disturbances.

elements: Defendant knowingly prevented or attempted to prevent a peace officer
From effecting an arrest
By using or threatening the use of physical force against the officer or another
enhancements: Use of a weapon during resistance
notes: Montana requires physical force or threat of physical force for resisting arrest. Mere verbal refusal or passive resistance may not be sufficient.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly obstructed, impaired, or prevented
The administration of law or other government function
By physical interference or obstacle
notes: Montana's obstruction statute is a felony, covering interference with judicial proceedings, law enforcement operations, and government functions.

elements: Defendant engaged in disorderly behavior in the presence of the court
Or violated a court order
Or willfully disobeyed a lawful process or order of the court
notes: Direct contempt (in court) can be punished summarily. Indirect contempt (violation of court order) requires notice and hearing.

offense_class: Not a criminal offense (protective custody only)
elements: Person is found in a public place in an intoxicated condition
And is unable to care for their own safety
notes: Montana decriminalized public intoxication. Intoxicated persons are placed in protective custody, not arrested. Treatment-focused approach under the Alcoholism and Drug Dependence Act.

offense_class: Felony (if underlying charge is felony); Misdemeanor (if underlying charge is misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or own recognizance
Defendant was required to appear before a court
Defendant purposely failed to appear as required
notes: Penalty matches the seriousness of the underlying offense. Court issues a bench warrant upon failure to appear.

elements: Defendant knowingly gave false information to a law enforcement officer
About an alleged offense or incident
With the purpose of inducing the officer to act
notes: Includes false reports of crimes and false emergency calls. Defendant may also be liable for costs of investigation and emergency response.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly communicated a threat
To commit any offense involving violence to any person
With the purpose of causing the person to be in sustained fear for their safety
enhancements: Threat against a public official or law enforcement officer
notes: Montana calls criminal threats 'intimidation.' It is a felony regardless of whether the threat is carried out.

elements: Defendant made a false statement under oath or equivalent affirmation
In an official proceeding
The statement was material to the proceeding
Defendant did not believe the statement to be true
enhancements: Perjury resulting in conviction of innocent person
notes: Montana requires proof that the false statement was material. Recantation before the statement substantially affected the proceeding is a defense.

statute_title: Bribery in Official and Political Matters
elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer upon a public servant
Any benefit as consideration for the public servant's decision, opinion, or action
In an official matter
notes: Both offering and accepting bribes are criminal offenses. Public servant includes any government official or employee.

elements: Defendant was in official detention
Defendant purposely removed themselves from the detention
Or failed to return to detention following a temporary leave
enhancements: Use of force or threat of force
Use of a weapon during escape
notes: Official detention includes any jail, prison, or lawful custody. Sentence for escape may be consecutive to the original sentence.

elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly subjected an animal to mistreatment or neglect
By overworking, torturing, tormenting, or cruelly beating the animal
Or by failing to provide necessary food, water, or shelter
enhancements: Aggravated animal cruelty (torture or killing — felony under § 45-8-217)
notes: Aggravated animal cruelty under § 45-8-217 is a felony punishable by up to 2 years. Animal fighting is separately prohibited.

penalty_max: Original suspended or deferred sentence may be revoked
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Court may revoke, continue, or modify probation. Graduated sanctions approach used for technical violations. Burden of proof is preponderance of the evidence.

elements: Defendant was released on parole or conditional release
Defendant violated a condition of parole
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
notes: Board of Pardons and Parole makes revocation decisions. Graduated sanctions used for technical violations. Montana uses a structured decision-making framework.

elements: Defendant, with the purpose of promoting or facilitating the commission of an offense
Solicited, aided, abetted, agreed, or attempted to aid another in the planning or commission
Of the offense
mandatory_minimum: Same as principal offense
notes: Montana's accountability statute holds accomplices criminally liable to the same extent as the principal. No distinction between principal and accessory at trial.

offense_class: Same maximum as the completed offense
elements: Defendant, with the purpose of committing a specific offense
Performed an act toward the commission of the offense
That constituted a substantial step toward commission
notes: Under Montana law, attempt carries the same maximum penalty as the completed offense. Voluntary abandonment before completion is an affirmative defense.

offense_class: Felony (if target offense is felony); Misdemeanor (if target offense is misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to engage in conduct constituting a crime
Defendant or a co-conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of the conspiracy
Defendant had the purpose that the crime be committed
notes: Montana conspiracy carries the same maximum penalty as the target offense. Withdrawal is a defense if defendant thwarted the conspiracy's success.
